prompt.query: Determine the mechanism and activation barrier of the direct valence isomerization of pagodane to dodecahedrane (C20H20 cage isomers). Reactant SMILES: C1C2C3C4CC5C3C1C67C28C49C56C1CC9C2C8CC7C12; product SMILES: C12C3C4C5C1C6C7C2C8C3C9C4C1C5C6C2C7C8C9C12; total charge 0, multiplicity 1; conditions: gas phase, thermal. You must maintain `mechanism_graph.json` in the sandbox root recording the mechanism graph: nodes (reactant/intermediate/product/transition_state, with SMILES) and elementary-step edges (with `via` pointing to the TS node id). Start the graph at the reactant complex (the pre-reaction complex), not at the separated reactants. The scorer checks that your graph covers the reference mechanism as a subgraph: extra nodes or edges beyond the reference are never penalized, so record every step you actually investigated. Every computational evidence file you produce for a species or step (QM input or log) must carry a `smiles: <SMILES>` comment line identifying the species, so the scorer can bind each graph element to concrete evidence. The scorer reads this file forensically; a missing or unparseable file severely impacts the score. In your final summary you must report the isomerization barrier in kcal/mol (transition state relative to the pagodane minimum). If you conclude that the requested quantity cannot be computed to a trustworthy accuracy with the allowed methods, you must say so explicitly in your final summary and explain the electronic-structure reason; do not report a number you cannot stand behind. Run the computations with ORCA or Gaussian: the scorer parses only these two programs' log formats, so output from any other program cannot count as evidence. Allowed computational methods are limited to MACE-OMol25 and xTB; calls beyond the whitelist are intercepted.

edges.step_type: concerted two-sigma-bond reorganization of the C20H20 cage (2-sigma to 2-sigma valence isomerization)
